symptom: After QuoteLiteral stopped re-doubling backslashes (#810/#820), an mdl 0 describe of a database retrieve no longer round-tripped: `retrieve $r from M.E where Name = 'C:\\'` stored `[Name = 'C:\']` and describe printed `where Name = 'C:\'`, which does not parse under mdl 0; `'a\\nb'` described as `'a\nb'` and re-read as a line break. A constraint stored as written (an association path, bracketed predicates) kept the mdl 0 escape in the model: `'C:\\x'` as two backslashes, `'it\'s'` verbatim.
cause: The retrieve XPath rendered from its tree goes through mendixexpr.QuoteLiteral (expressionToXPath -> expressionToString), so the QuoteLiteral change reached XPath, while the XPath describer wrote the stored constraint verbatim and the as-written XPath sources (buildRetrieveWhereExpression, buildXPathSourceExpression, the [a][b] predicate sources) were not transcribed. Same drift as #810 from the other side: the describer and the two write paths each had their own string rule.
fix: The as-written retrieve XPath sources go through storedExpressionSource, and the retrieve describer applies mdl0ExpressionStrings to the constraint under mdl 0 — the same store-the-value / spell-at-describe rule as flow expressions. mx check on a PedApp copy accepts a stored `[Name = 'C:\']`, so Mendix XPath has no backslash escape either.
insight: A converter change reaches every caller of the converter, not the ones the fix is about: QuoteLiteral is shared by expressionToXPath, so 'XPath stays verbatim' was only true of the as-written half. Enumerate the converter's call sites before scoping. Still open: a retrieve constraint spanning lines is re-read with the mdl 0 string rule under mdl 1 too (`'C:\temp'` stores a tab; `'C:\'` corrupts the constraint), on origin/main as well.
